Structural Limits of Quantum Superposition and the Principle of Equivalence\n   ID: iewyqth8cdrv\n   2025\n   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.17958496\n   Abstract: The conceptual tension between quantum superposition and the principle of equivalence has long been regarded as a signal of deep incompatbility between quantum mechanics and gravitation. In this work, a different perspective is developed. Rather than postulating additional dynamics or modifications of established theories, we introduce a structural criterion for representational existence and argue that both quantum superposition and the principle of equivalence are effective properties of a restricted representational regime. The analysis is formulated in terms of Hilbert bundles defined over a general configuration domain, without presupposing the existence of a globally trivializable state space. Superposition is shown to require the existence of admissible global sections of the associated representational bundle, while the principle of equivalence depends on the simultaneous availability of coherent local projections. When these structural conditions fail, neither superposition nor equivalence is physically well-defined, without invoking any dynamical collapse or violation of quantum evolution. From this standpoint, gravitational scenarios commonly associated with objective collapse are reinterpreted as regimes of representational non-existence rather than as sites of new physical processes.                       "abstract": "The conceptual tension between quantum superposition and the principle of equivalence has long been regarded as a signal of deep incompatbility between quantum mechanics and gravitation. In particular, approaches invoking gravitationally induced objective collapse interpret the breakdown of superposition as the manifestation of a new physical process driven by spacetime geometry. In this work, a different perspective is developed. Rather than postulating additional dynamics or modifications of established theories, we introduce a structural criterion for representational existence and argue that both quantum superposition and the principle of equivalence are effective properties of a restricted representational regime. The analysis is formulated in terms of Hilbert bundles defined over a general configuration domain, without presupposing the existence of a globally trivializable state space. Superposition is shown to require the existence of admissible global sections of the associated representational bundle, while the principle of equivalence depends on the simultaneous availability of coherent local projections. When these structural conditions fail, neither superposition nor equivalence is physically well-defined, without invoking any dynamical collapse or violation of quantum evolution. From this standpoint, gravitational scenarios commonly associated with objective collapse are reinterpreted as regimes of representational non-existence rather than as sites of new physical processes. The apparent conflict between quantum mechanics and gravitation is thus dissolved by a precise delimitation of the domains of validity of their foundational principles. The report delves into scientific models such as the Big Bounce, Oscillating Universe, and Conformal Cyclic Cosmology (CCC), each proposing that the universe undergoes repeated cycles of expansion and contraction rather than originating from a single event.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The document begins by outlining the limitations of the Big Bang theory, particularly the unresolved issue of the initial singularity where current physics breaks down. In contrast, cyclical models reinterpret the Big Bang as a transitional event-a bridge between cosmic epochs-rather than the absolute beginning of everything.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Key scientific models are explored in detail:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Big Bounce Theory:&lt;/strong&gt;&nbsp;Suggests the universe's expansion follows a prior contraction phase, with quantum effects preventing a true singularity and enabling a cosmic \"bounce.\"&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Oscillating Universe Models:&lt;/strong&gt;&nbsp;Propose endless cycles of expansion and contraction, with modern variants addressing challenges like entropy accumulation through mechanisms such as brane collisions (Steinhardt-Turok model) or phantom energy (Baum-Frampton model).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Conformal Cyclic Cosmology (CCC):&lt;/strong&gt;&nbsp;Developed by Roger Penrose, this model connects the infinite future of one universe to the Big Bang of the next via conformal geometry, potentially leaving observable imprints in the cosmic microwave background.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;The report also examines the philosophical implications of a cyclical cosmos, discussing concepts like eternal return-the idea that all events recur infinitely-and the anthropic principle, which suggests that repeated cycles increase the likelihood of life's emergence.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;By integrating scientific analysis with philosophical reflection, the report presents the cyclical universe as a compelling framework for understanding cosmic history and the potential for life's recurrence across epochs.
